tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: ACME Solar Holdings Limited, Solar Power Developers Association and Avaada Clean Energy Private Limited (Petitioners) filed a petition dated May 02, 2019 under Article 226 of the Constitution of India before the High Court of Delhi against the Union of India (Ministry of Finance), Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (Respondents), challenging the validity of (i) the explanation to serial no. 234 of Notification No. 1/2017 – Central Tax (Rate) dated June 28, 2017 inserted pursuant to Notification No. 24/2018 – Central Tax (Rate) dated December 31, 2018, and (ii) the explanation to serial no. 38 of Notification No. 11/2017 – Central Tax (Rate) dated June 28, 2017 inserted pursuant to Notification No. 27/2018 – Central Tax (Rate) dated December 31, 2018 (Impugned Notifications), alleging that such Impugned Notifications were illegal and violative of Articles 14, 19(1)(g), 246 and 265 of the Constitution of India and Section 15 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. The Impugned Notifications provide that under a solar power generating system contract, the value of goods shall be deemed to be 70% and taxable at 5%, while the value of services shall be deemed to be 30% and taxable at 18%, which significantly differs from the actual split of 93:7. The matter is currently pending. The matter was heard on November 20, 2024, December 13, 2024, March 03, 2025, and May 08, 2025. (Last disclosure-The next date of hearing was November 17, 2025).
